Input1 gives existing up-stepping platforms, return slope and distant blue-water scale; do NOT copy its inappropriate mouth-baleen roof. Input2 chapter cutaway supplies intended anatomy: DORSAL PAIRED BLOWHOLE location ABOVE a visibly solid intact hard-palate slab, reached around its left side via an OLD LATERAL WOUND. There is no open direct mouth-to-nose hole. ALL underwater, no air pocket, sea surface, sky, exhaling, geyser or breathing whale.
Compose a broad room with VERTICAL exploration inside it (landscape 4:3). Lower left approach is a rugged old skull-side wound and red maintenance tether, curving around thick solid creamy skull mass. Three unequal rooted ascending shelves cross to mid/right; substantial irregular roots join the same sidewalls rather than identical floating mushroom platforms. The first shelf low-left, second center, third upper-right; top of room clearly shows TWO large separate DARK NASAL RIMS embedded in dorsal tissue, high above and behind the observation ledge. Keep a hefty bone/soft-tissue divider between them so they read paired, not generic cave windows. Solid palate below nasal space fills the lower body of the painting; return ramp runs along its top into lower-left wound. No playable hole cut straight through it.
The highest platform near right holds ONE small existing SEALED FUNGAL MODULE in a shallow shell cradle, a modest engraved flat capsule, not a magical pearl. Behind far-right top ledge a closed slit with red cord is only the existing far-side return latch hint, not an open new exit. No enemies, no additional rewards. One microscopic original diver on first shelf, ivory round head with ONE dark lens, short teal cape, U-shaped two-pronged resonator, amber enclosed lamp, no ghost poses.
Material: dense chalk-ivory skull surface becomes grey-violet longitudinal nasal folds, subdued calcareous growth at ledge joints, dark teal water with a distant small fish school and a few tiny side bubbles. Absolutely NO baleen curtains in nasal chamber, NO upper jaw teeth, no ribcage in nose. Pale cyan light scatters within dark water, soft amber sealed biological light marks lower left rest niche. Rich matte gouache brushwork, large quiet far masses, crisp playable rim, soft dark foreground framing corners, organic asymmetry. Do not tile oval holes over all surfaces. No labels, arrows, HUD, borders, separate panels, horns/knight, nail/sword or masonry.
